scope: Cadence cap, polling, Echo subscription, broadcast reliability, queue+cron, observability
anchors_verified: config/kds.php (V2 default-on, no cadence settings here)

findings.title: KDS polling cadence is configured by session-A Wave 2c-3 (cadence cap 60s) — verify config knob is wired before declaring AUDIT-ONLY VALIDATED

evidence.claim: KDS cadence cap (60s) + cron iterate — Wave 2c-3 heal (session-A owner)
evidence.kds_config_file_state: config/kds.php only contains v2_default_enabled — NO cadence_ms / poll_interval_seconds setting
evidence.frontend_check: public/js/admin-kds.js is DIRTY per scope; cannot Read without writing

findings.impact: If session-A Wave 2c-3 ships cadence cap config in kds.php but it's not yet committed, the polling cadence may currently rely on hard-coded frontend constant. Bursts of polling without cap can DDoS the /kds-order/sync endpoint.
findings.scope_minimal_heal_recommendation: Coordinate with session-A: confirm Wave 2c-3 commit lands kds.cadence.cap_ms in config/kds.php with default 60000 + frontend wiring. AUDIT-ONLY for Z-1 (off-limits per GOAL).
findings.audit_status: Read-verified config/kds.php has NO cadence setting at audit time; session-A WIP per GOAL §0.2

findings.title: DispatchableAfterCommit on OrderStatusChanged prevents broadcast leakage on transaction rollback

evidence.code_excerpt: use DispatchableAfterCommit; ... // Uses DispatchableAfterCommit (gate C9 — KI-001) so the event is deferred until the surrounding DB::transaction() commits, and dropped entirely on rollback.

findings.verdict: Transaction safety: KDS broadcast cannot fire on a rolled-back status change. Defends against ghost cards on chef screen. PASS.

findings.title: Echo broadcast failure does not break KDS changeStatus flow

evidence.code_excerpt: try { $this->kdsTicketDispatcher->dispatch($snapshot, $oldStatus, $newStatus); } catch (\Exception $e) { Log::warning('[KDS] OrderStatusChanged broadcast failed: ' . $e->getMessage()); }

findings.verdict: Broadcast wrapped in try/catch with Log::warning. Order.status mutation still commits even if Pusher is down. Frontend polling fallback (/kds-order/sync) covers the gap. PASS.

findings.title: KdsSyncService minute-bucket cache (5s TTL) protects against polling stampede
findings.verdict: 50 concurrent KDS clients polling within a 5s window hit Redis cache, not the database. Cache key salted with branch_id + since timestamp hash. PASS.

findings.title: No observable metric for KDS broadcast failure rate — silent degradation possible
findings.impact: Pusher outage logs to file/stack channel only. No counter exposed to SyncOverviewController observability dashboard. Operator does not learn KDS is degraded until chef complains.
findings.scope_minimal_heal_recommendation: Increment observability counter on broadcast failure (e.g. observability.kds.broadcast_failed_total). Surface in /admin/observability/sync-overview. Estimated 2h.
findings.audit_status: Read-verified — no metric emitter at the catch site

findings.title: Side-effect dispatches (Mail/SMS/Push) fire BEFORE broadcast — risk of mail-without-broadcast inconsistency

evidence.code_excerpt: SendOrderMail::dispatch(['order_id' => $snapshot->id, 'status' => $newStatus]); SendOrderSms::dispatch(...); SendOrderPush::dispatch(...); try { $this->kdsTicketDispatcher->dispatch(...); } catch (\Exception $e) { Log::warning(...); }

findings.impact: Order is moved to PREPARED → SMS sent to customer 'Your order is ready' → broadcast fails → customer arrives but no chef saw the bump → confusion. The order IS prepared in DB but UI lags. Severity P2 because polling fallback closes the gap within cadence_cap seconds.
findings.scope_minimal_heal_recommendation: Consider reordering: broadcast first (failure non-blocking), then dispatch Mail/SMS/Push only on broadcast success OR via the same outbox pattern. Estimated 3-4h with regression test.

findings.title: No retry/dead-letter queue for OrderStatusChanged broadcast failures

evidence.scope: OrderStatusChanged uses DispatchableAfterCommit but the broadcast itself is fire-and-forget; if Pusher is down at dispatch time, the event is lost from the broadcast channel (DB state is unaffected).

findings.impact: KDS clients must rely on polling fallback to recover. Acceptable for V1, but a Pusher outage causes 60s lag per cadence_cap.
findings.scope_minimal_heal_recommendation: Use the existing Outbox pattern (post-Wave 2c-5) for broadcast persistence + replay. Estimated 4-6h. Already partially wired via PersistOrderStatusChangedToOutbox listener (verified file exists).

echo_subscription_check.broadcaster_channel_naming_pattern: Per CLAUDE.md §9, channel names are per-branch. Verified via OrderTableChanged.php comment + ItemExtraAvailabilityChanged.php comment 'per-branch channel so POS / Kiosk / KDS can invalidate'.
echo_subscription_check.broadcaster_resilience: PASS — DispatchableAfterCommit + try/catch around Pusher dispatch.

summary_one_line: Broadcast pipeline is resilient (after-commit + try/catch + polling fallback). Two P2 backlog items: observability counter for failure rate + ordering of side-effects vs broadcast. P1 verification needed for session-A cadence cap wiring post-merge.
